title: Hosting decision playbook — low-latency POC with hybrid fallback
body:
Executive summary:

This note captures a compact playbook for a mid-sized enterprise POC where the primary success metric is perceived interactive latency (95th < 400ms) on 2–4M tokens/mo. Customer constraints: EU data residency, strong SLA expectation for peak business hours (09:00–18:00 CET), and potential bursty traffic from a web chat widget.

Goal: deliver repeatable recommendations and a runnable plan that lets sales and engineering sign off on a single POC architecture within 2 weeks. Keep options scoped: Hosted, Dedicated, Private (VPC/on-prem) and a hybrid fallback strategy.

Context & constraints (notes):
- Customer: mid-market fintech, no on-prem requirement but FIPS/KMS integration required for keys.
- Traffic: baseline 30 qps during business hours (100–200ms think time between messages), bursts to 150 qps for short windows.
- Model: Llama2-13B quantized to 4-bit or a 14B open model; inference cost sensitivity but quality-sensitive.
- Network: customer front-end in EU region, must avoid cross-region egress where possible.
- Security: audit logs & VPC peering preferred; SSO for admin console.

Candidate architectures (short sketches):

1) Hosted-first (fastest to ship)
- Description: POC uses Redwood Hosted API in eu-west region, customer uses standard API keys with region restriction + KMS integration (Bring-your-key via API token vault).
- Pros: quickest onboarding, no infra ops, Redwood takes autoscaling and fallbacks to regionally proximate pools. Built-in observability and cost telemetry out of the box.
- Cons: potential unit-cost delta vs dedicated; egress if customer proxies traffic poorly; limited control for strict isolation or custom kernels.
- Risk notes: need to validate BYK (bring-your-key) compatibility for customer's KMS; confirm audit retention window.

2) Dedicated-reserved (predictable perf)
- Description: Reserve dedicated GPU pool (1x A10g equivalent initial), pin model to quantized variant, route customer traffic to dedicated pool using tenant tag. Redwood manages capacity.
- Pros: consistent latency, lower per-token cost at moderate commit levels, isolation for noisy neighbors, easy scaling plan.
- Cons: reservation lead time; peak-burst handling requires burst policy (map to shared pools) — requires explicit SLA/cost conversation.
- Risk notes: must size KV cache memory for conversational workloads; if session affinity is required, include sticky routing.

3) Private (VPC or on-prem)
- Description: Deploy Redwood Private control plane and inference nodes in customer's cloud VPC (or on-prem appliance). Full network control and KMS/HSM integration.
- Pros: meets strict compliance/residency; complete control of data path; no cross-tenant concerns.
- Cons: longer setup time (2–6 weeks depending on customer infra), ops burden for customer if they choose on-prem, higher minimum cost for small POC.
- Risk notes: baseline telemetry may require connector configuration; ensure approval from infra/security for inbound networking and NAT rules.

Hybrid recommendation (POC-specific):
- Primary: Hosted-first for day 0 testing and functional validation (two days integration).
- Secondary: Dedicated-reserved as the default POC architecture if latency variability or cost is a blocker for customer signoff. Provision dedicated pool with automatic fallback to hosted shared pools for bursts or capacity issues.
- Private: Only if customer signs an enterprise contract or requires formal isolation/KMS in-scope at POC time. Otherwise, schedule Private readiness as follow-up milestone.

Why hybrid:
- Speed of hosted to validate UX and model outputs quickly with real traffic.
- Predictable latency/cost from dedicated for a clean customer demo and SLA adherence during evaluation week.
- Fallback keeps the application resilient during unexpected traffic spikes or dedicated pool drain.

Configuration checklist (what we must agree on before POC begins):
- Model artifact and quantization variant (exact name/hash).
- Traffic routing policy: session affinity? cookie header? use request id mapping.
- SLO targets: p95 latency < 400ms, error rate < 1%, token cost cap.
- Data residency checkpoint: log retention, telemetry scrub rules, and KMS key lifecycle.
- Burst policy: accept fallback to hosted shared pools OR pre-warm additional containers for X minutes.
- Observability: which dashboards (console share link), trace sampling (50% of requests), and alert hooks (PagerDuty/Slack).

Simple cost sketch (back-of-envelope):
- Hosted-only: baseline estimate $3.5–4.5k/month for 2–4M tokens depending on model and streaming vs non-streaming.
- Dedicated (small reserve): $9–12k/month committed + marginal lower per-token. For a 4-week POC window consider pro-rata commit or short-term burst credits.
- Private: initial onboarding + infra sizing (est. $25k one-time engineering + infra costs) — typically not justified for short POC.

Routing and failure modes (operational playbook):
- Normal: requests -> regional API gateway -> dedicated tenant pool.
- If dedicated pool > 80% utilization for 3m: trigger autoscale or route new sessions to hosted shared pool (tagged fallback).
- If region outage (cloud provider): automatic route to next-closest region with cross-region privacy disclaimer; for regulated customers, we MUST avoid this unless pre-approved.
- If model regression observed (quality vs baseline): circuit-break to previous model variant, notify SE and customer success.

Validation plan & success criteria (POC acceptance):
- Technical: p95 latency target met during business-hour window for 3/5 test days; error rate < 1%.
- Quality: blind eval on 100 core prompts, automated BLEU/ROUGE-ish checks where applicable, and 10 manual QA user journeys approved by customer SME.
- Business: cost-per-active-session within agreed budget threshold and product-team signoff on UX latency.

Rollout steps (two-week POC cadence):
- Day 0–2: Hosted integration, smoke tests, model sanity checks, telemetry baseline.
- Day 3–5: Provision dedicated pool, route subset (10%) of traffic to dedicated, compare latency/cost metrics.
- Day 6–10: Ramp dedicated to 100% for business hours, run load tests at burst levels, simulate failure modes (force fallback).
- Day 11–14: Evaluation window, customer demos, handoff docs and cost forecast.

Operational attachments (practical items):
- Sample routing config snippet to use in customer front-end (copy/paste in their app):
  - header: X-Redwood-Tenant: <tenant-id>
  - prefer_region: eu-west-1
  - prefer_model: llm-14b-q4

- Minimal healthcheck endpoints for customer infra: /health/rls (returns cached-kv-size, queue-depth, model-variant).

ASCII network sketch (very rough):
  [Customer FE in EU] -> [Regional CDN/Edge] -> [Redwood Edge GW (eu-west)] -> {Dedicated Pool (eu-west) OR Hosted Shared Pool (eu-west)} -> [KV cache / model nodes]

Open questions / decisions needed from customer (action items):
- Confirm KMS provider + BYK requirements and keys accessible for Redwood control plane.
- Acceptable fallback behavior if dedicated pool is saturated? (Must we pause new sessions or route to shared?)
- Compliance: does the customer require physical isolation or is VPC+audit sufficient?
- Billing: are pro-rata reserved capacity charges acceptable or do they prefer usage-based for POC?

Team action items (owner initials):
- MR: prepare dedicated pool sizing template and cost options (due in 48h).
- LC: draft demo script and telemetry dashboard snapshot (due in 72h).
- PP: confirm BYK interaction with security team and produce KMS checklist (due in 5 business days).

Notes to self / stylistic reminders for SEs delivering this POC: keep the narrative simple for the customer—start with Hosted demo, then show measurable improvements after switching to Dedicated. Avoid heavy Private discussion unless customer asks; highlight that Private is available but has nontrivial setup time.

References & quick links (internal):
- Slack thread: #se-poc-hosting (search "fintech-eu-poc")
- Template: /templates/poc-cost-breakdown-brief.md
- Eval harness PR: github.com/redwood/evals/pull/479

End of playbook.

-- MR (notes inline during SE workshop 2025-11-12)

Unresolved: possible need to pre-warm KV cache for cold-start heavy sessions; confirm memory footprint per-session for llm-14b-q4.
